newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fruit, veges lead NZ food prices lower in May.
newsitem.headline: Fruit, veges lead NZ food prices lower in May.

text.p: The Food Price Index fell by 0.8 percent in May 1997, the first fall in food prices since December 1996, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
May's price falls follow an April increase of 0.1 percent.
The index is now 1.7 percent higher than in May 1996.
SNZ said the fruit and vegetable subgroup was the main contributor to falling food prices, decreasing an unseasonal 7.1 percent in May.

"The largest single factor behind the fall was a drop in tomato prices," SNZ said. "However, our recent Indian summer' and the better growing conditions for fruit and vegetables may also have influenced price decreases in vegetables like cauliflower, broccoli and lettuce."
SNZ said excluding fresh fruit and vegetables (which is a subgroup of the wider fruit and vegetable subgroup), the food price index rose 0.2 percent in May.
The fruit and vegetable subgroup is now 1.6 percent higher than in May 1996. In contrast, overall meat, fish and poultry prices increased by 1.2 percent in May 1997.
SNZ said the most significant rises were in mince, steak and sausages. It said the meat, fish and poultry subgroup was 2.7 percent higher than in May 1996, its tenth consecutive annual increase.

Grocery food prices remained unchanged during May 1997, but the grocery subgroup is now 1.6 percent higher than in May 1996. "For the first time since November 1995, the restaurant meals and ready-to-eat food subgroup recorded a monthly decrease," SNZ said.
"The May 1997 decrease of 0.1 percent was driven by fall in prices of restaurant meals."
The subgroup is 1.5 percent higher than in May 1996.
SNZ said 14 of the 15 regional centres showed decreases in overall food prices in May 1997, with Nelson the only region to record and increase.
The largest fall in food prices, down 2.0 percent, was recorded in New Plymouth.
